_about: Likely causes for the Monitor tab's incidents. incidents.py decides WHICH cause applies (rules in code); this file says what it means and what to check. Edit the text freely; keep the keys. 'where' is the host to run a check on. Commands are for a person to run: nothing here is run automatically.

MONRX_DOWN.title: monitor-receiver (high side) is not passing monitoring on
MONRX_DOWN.explain: Nothing from the low side can reach the console's Monitor tab while monitor-receiver is down, so the low side looks silent even if it is fine. Chat is not affected: it has its own receiver and port.

checks.do: cd high && docker compose up -d monitor-receiver

RECEIVER_DOWN.title: the chat receiver (high side) is not reporting
RECEIVER_DOWN.explain: The receiver posts its counters every 30 s; none have arrived. Chat messages are not reaching the console (or the Gotham feed) while it is down. Monitoring is not affected.

LEFT_SILENT.title: nothing is arriving from this low-side host
LEFT_SILENT.explain: signal-monitor's packets stopped and no chat has arrived since either. From the high side it can't be told apart: the low-side host is down, its containers are stopped, or the diode is not passing traffic. signal-cli and the subscribers show UNKNOWN for that reason.

checks.do: check the diode's status for the chat rooms' routes and the monitoring route (CHAT|MONITOR)

MONITOR_ONLY_SILENT.title: signal-monitor (or its diode port) is silent, but chat still arrives
MONITOR_ONLY_SILENT.explain: Chat packets kept arriving after signal-monitor went quiet, so the low-side host, signal-cli, a subscriber and the diode's chat flow are working. The problem is signal-monitor itself, or the monitoring flow (the monitoring route) through the diode.

checks.do: check the monitoring route (CHAT|MONITOR) on the diode

CONTAINER_STOPPED.title: a relay container was stopped on purpose
CONTAINER_STOPPED.explain: Docker reports a clean stop (exit code 0 or 143, or 137 without running out of memory): someone or something ran docker stop, docker compose stop/down, or a host shutdown. It did not crash. If it's the subscriber, its group's messages wait in signal-cli (up to 1000, in memory) and are relayed when it starts again, unless signal-cli restarts in the meantime.

checks.do: was this planned? (maintenance, an update, a test)

CONTAINER_CRASHED.title: a relay container crashed
CONTAINER_CRASHED.explain: Docker reports the container's program ended with an error (a non-zero exit code other than 137/143). The last lines of its log say why. restart: unless-stopped normally starts it again; if it stays down, it may fail on every start.

CONTAINER_OOM.title: a relay container ran out of memory
CONTAINER_OOM.explain: Docker killed the container because it went over its memory limit (mem_limit in low/docker-compose.yml). It will likely happen again until the limit is raised or the cause (for example a large backlog) is gone.

CONTAINER_RESTARTING.title: a relay container keeps restarting
CONTAINER_RESTARTING.explain: Docker has restarted the container more than once recently: it starts, fails, and is started again. Each restart interrupts what it does (a subscriber reconnects and signal-cli resends what it has kept).

MONITOR_DISK_LOW.title: the low-side host is low on disk space
MONITOR_DISK_LOW.explain: signal-monitor reports less free space than DISK_LOW_PCT on the disk holding low/ (account data, logs). signal-cli and the subscriber can fail to save their state when it fills up.

CERT_EXPIRING.title: a certificate expires soon
CERT_EXPIRING.explain: A TLS certificate (signal-cli's gateway, the subscriber's or signal-monitor's) expires within CERT_WARN_DAYS. When it expires, that link stops: the subscriber can't read messages, or signal-monitor can't check signal-cli.

CLI_UNREACHABLE.title: signal-cli is not running (or not reachable)
CLI_UNREACHABLE.explain: signal-monitor can't connect to signal-cli's gateway at all: the container is stopped or crashed, or (split setup) the address in SIGNAL_TARGETS is wrong. Its subscribers lose their stream too.

checks.do: cd low && docker compose up -d signal

CLI_GATEWAY_CLOSED.title: signal-cli's gateway refuses signal-monitor's certificate
CLI_GATEWAY_CLOSED.explain: The connection opens, then the gateway closes it without answering. Usually the client certificate's name (signal-monitor) is not a line in low/gateway/clients.conf. signal-cli itself may be fine: check whether the subscribers are connected.

checks.do: grep -v '^#' low/gateway/clients.conf   # its certificate's name must be a line here (signal-monitor: with check)

CLI_TLS_FAILED.title: the secure connection to signal-cli fails
CLI_TLS_FAILED.explain: The TLS handshake fails: an expired certificate, a certificate from another CA, or a host name in SIGNAL_TARGETS that is not on signal-cli's server certificate.

CLI_TIMEOUT.title: signal-cli does not answer in time
CLI_TIMEOUT.explain: The gateway accepts the connection but the health check gets no answer within 10 s: signal-cli is hung, overloaded or out of memory.

CLI_HTTP_ERROR.title: signal-cli answers the health check with an error
CLI_HTTP_ERROR.explain: signal-cli is running and reachable, but /api/v1/check did not return OK. Its log says why.

CLI_DOWN.title: signal-cli is down
CLI_DOWN.explain: signal-monitor reports signal-cli down (no more specific reason was sent).

SUB_STOPPED.title: a subscriber stopped reporting
SUB_STOPPED.explain: signal-monitor has had no status from the subscriber for 35 s: the container is stopped or crashed, or (split setup) it can't reach signal-monitor on UDP 6520. While it is stopped, its group's messages are not relayed (signal-cli keeps the last 1000 in memory).

checks.do: cd low && docker compose up -d subscriber

SUB_GATEWAY_CLOSED.title: signal-cli's gateway refuses the subscriber
SUB_GATEWAY_CLOSED.explain: signal-cli is up (signal-monitor's check works), but it closes the subscriber's connection: usually the subscriber's certificate name is not a line in low/gateway/clients.conf. No messages are relayed until it connects.

checks.do: grep -v '^#' low/gateway/clients.conf   # its certificate's name must be a line here (signal-monitor: with check)

SUB_TLS_FAILED.title: the subscriber's secure connection to signal-cli fails
SUB_TLS_FAILED.explain: signal-cli is up, but the subscriber's TLS handshake fails: its certificate expired or is from another CA, or SIGNAL_URL uses a name that is not on signal-cli's certificate.

SUB_UNREACHABLE.title: the subscriber can't reach signal-cli
SUB_UNREACHABLE.explain: signal-monitor reaches signal-cli, but the subscriber does not: its SIGNAL_URL points somewhere else, or (split setup) the network between the hosts blocks it.

SUB_NOT_CONNECTED.title: a subscriber is not connected to signal-cli
SUB_NOT_CONNECTED.explain: The subscriber runs and reports, but its event stream to signal-cli is down. It reconnects every 3 s on its own.

STARTING.title: the low side is starting up
STARTING.explain: Parts report that they have just started and are not connected yet. This normally clears within a minute.

checks.do: wait a minute; if it doesn't clear, check the part's log

QUEUE_BACKLOG.title: messages are queuing in a subscriber
QUEUE_BACKLOG.explain: More than 100 messages are waiting to be sent across the diode. Usually a burst (signal-cli resending after a restart) that drains on its own at the PACE setting.

DIODE_LOSS.title: the diode is losing packets
DIODE_LOSS.explain: Monitoring packets arrive, but some in the numbering are missing. Chat on the same path is probably losing packets too (the receiver's lost counter and the 'lost' notices in the chat).

checks.do: the receiver tile: lost and packets missing

UNCLEAR.title: no single likely cause
UNCLEAR.explain: The rules found no known pattern. Look at the events of the parts involved, oldest first.

checks.do: the Events log on the Monitor tab, filtered to warnings and errors

SIGNAL_UNREACHABLE.title: signal-cli can't reach Signal's servers
SIGNAL_UNREACHABLE.explain: signal-cli runs, but has no working connection to Signal's servers (no keep-alive answered for 2 min). Nothing new comes in. New messages wait on Signal's servers and are delivered when it reconnects, so nothing is lost by waiting. Usual causes: this host's internet, a firewall or proxy blocking outgoing HTTPS, or Signal itself. Not DNS alone: Signal's library does its own lookups and has fallback addresses (a hosts-file test still connected). 'last failure' is usually CONNECT_FAILED (Signal's library hides the lower reason); signal-cli's log has the full line.

checks.do: curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://chat.signal.org/   # any code = this host can reach Signal (-k: Signal has its own CA)
ask: was a firewall, proxy or network change made around the time it started?

SIGNAL_RECONNECTING.title: signal-cli lost its connection to Signal's servers, reconnecting
SIGNAL_RECONNECTING.explain: signal-cli's connection to Signal dropped and it is retrying (100 ms, doubling to at most 51 s). Short drops happen; after 2 min it becomes 'can't reach Signal's servers'.

SIGNAL_FLAPPING.title: signal-cli's connection to Signal keeps dropping
SIGNAL_FLAPPING.explain: More than 5 reconnects to Signal's servers in an hour. Messages still arrive between drops, but late. Often an unstable network path, a proxy cutting long connections, or NAT timeouts.

checks.do: docker logs --since 1h signal-cli 2>&1 | grep -c 'Connection closed unexpectedly'

DEVICE_UNLINKED.title: Signal no longer accepts this signal-cli (unlinked or deregistered)
DEVICE_UNLINKED.explain: Signal refused signal-cli's login: the linked device was removed on the phone, or the number was registered on another device. It never recovers on its own and NOTHING arrives until someone fixes it. Messages sent meanwhile are not delivered to this device.

checks.do: Phone (main device): Settings > Linked devices: is this device still listed?
Relink or re-register: high/docs/register-account.md (a person with the phone is needed)

CLIENT_EXPIRED.title: Signal refuses this signal-cli version as too old
CLIENT_EXPIRED.explain: Signal's servers reject this signal-cli release. Nothing arrives until signal-cli is updated. Signal does this a few months after a release.

checks.do: set the new image in low/docker-compose.yml, then: cd low && docker compose up -d signal

RECEIVE_STALLED.title: signal-cli's receive loop is stuck
RECEIVE_STALLED.explain: signal-cli answers its health check, but the loop that takes messages from Signal has not run for 3 min (it runs at least once a minute). Nothing new comes in. A restart of signal-cli usually clears it; check first that the subscriber is connected and caught up (queue 0), so nothing in signal-cli's memory is lost.

checks.do: cd low && docker compose restart signal

CLOCK_SKEW.title: this host's clock is far off from Signal's
CLOCK_SKEW.explain: Signal's servers say this host's clock is more than a day off. Signal may refuse requests, and times on messages look wrong.

JVM_MEMORY.title: signal-cli's Java memory is almost full
JVM_MEMORY.explain: After garbage collection, over 90% of signal-cli's Java memory is still in use. It may slow down, then run out of memory and crash.

STORAGE_ERROR.title: signal-cli has database errors in its account data
STORAGE_ERROR.explain: signal-cli's own database (low/signal-data) gave errors: disk full, wrong permissions, or a damaged file. Messages may fail to be stored or decrypted.

EVENT_DROPPED.title: signal-cli received messages it could not pass on
EVENT_DROPPED.explain: signal-cli got a message from Signal but could not turn it into an event, so it never reached the subscriber. It is lost for the relay.

DECRYPT_FAILED.title: signal-cli could not decrypt some messages
DECRYPT_FAILED.explain: Messages arrived that signal-cli could not decrypt (a broken session with that sender). The sender's app usually resends; if it keeps happening for one person, their session needs a reset.

UNTRUSTED_IDENTITY.title: messages from a sender whose safety number changed
UNTRUSTED_IDENTITY.explain: A sender's safety number changed (new phone or reinstall). signal-cli holds their messages back until the new identity is trusted.

checks.do: ./image/signalctl cli -a NUM listIdentities   # signal stopped; see high/docs/image.md

HANDLE_ERROR.title: signal-cli had errors handling received messages
HANDLE_ERROR.explain: signal-cli logged errors while handling received messages. See its log for which.

GATEWAY_FULL.title: signal-cli's gateway turned connections away (all in use)
GATEWAY_FULL.explain: The TLS gateway in front of signal-cli allows 32 connections; it was full and refused more. Something may be opening connections without closing them.

checks.do: docker logs --since 1h signal-cli 2>&1 | grep -i gateway | tail -20

GATEWAY_REFUSED.title: a client with a certificate signal-cli doesn't allow tried to connect
GATEWAY_REFUSED.explain: The TLS gateway refused a client: its certificate is not from our CA or its name is not a line in low/gateway/clients.conf. A wrong setting, an old certificate, or someone probing.

RPC_BLOCKED.title: signal-cli's gateway blocked calls that are not allowed
RPC_BLOCKED.explain: Someone with a valid certificate asked the gateway for something not on its read-only list (e.g. send). It was blocked; the one-way rule held.

SENDER_DEAD.title: a subscriber's sender stopped
SENDER_DEAD.explain: The part of the subscriber that sends messages through the diode stopped. It still reads from signal-cli, so messages pile up and nothing is relayed. A restart resends from the saved position.

checks.do: cd low && docker compose restart subscriber

SENDER_STALLED.title: a subscriber stopped sending while messages wait
SENDER_STALLED.explain: Messages are waiting in the subscriber, but it has sent nothing for over a minute. Its sender is stuck.

checks.do: cd low && docker compose restart subscriber

SEND_FAILED.title: a subscriber can't send UDP packets
SEND_FAILED.explain: Sending to the diode failed (no route, a bad UDP_DEST, the network down). Those messages did not leave this host and are lost for the relay; they are in the subscriber's sent log.

EVENTS_MISSED.title: events from signal-cli never reached a subscriber
EVENTS_MISSED.explain: signal-cli numbers its events without gaps; the subscriber saw a jump, so those events never reached it (e.g. it fell more than 1000 behind and signal-cli dropped the oldest). They are lost for the relay.

CLI_RESTART_LOSS.title: signal-cli restarted while a subscriber was not connected
CLI_RESTART_LOSS.explain: signal-cli keeps received messages in memory only (it has already confirmed them to Signal). It restarted while the subscriber was away, so what it received in that window is lost. The tile and the event give the window.

checks.do: docker logs --since 1h signal-subscriber 2>&1 | grep -i 'may be lost'

MESSAGE_SKIPPED.title: a subscriber skipped messages it could not convert
MESSAGE_SKIPPED.explain: A message could not be turned into CEF and was skipped (not relayed). It is in signal-cli's history only. See the subscriber's log for why.

SENDER_ERROR.title: a subscriber failed to send messages in an unexpected way
SENDER_ERROR.explain: An error nobody foresaw happened while sending; that message was skipped and the sender carried on.

WRITE_FAILED.title: a subscriber can't write its files
WRITE_FAILED.explain: It could not write its sent log or its saved position (low/logs): disk full or permissions. Relaying carries on, but after a restart messages may be sent again.

STREAM_STALLED.title: a subscriber's event stream got stuck
STREAM_STALLED.explain: Nothing came from signal-cli for 45 s, not even its keep-alives (every 15 s), so the subscriber reconnected. Once is a hiccup; again and again means a network device or signal-cli is holding the connection.

QUEUE_SLOW.title: messages wait a long time in a subscriber
QUEUE_SLOW.explain: The oldest waiting message has waited over 5 minutes: the subscriber sends slower than messages arrive.

PACKET_TOO_BIG.title: a subscriber sent packets over the size limit
PACKET_TOO_BIG.explain: A packet was over 1472 bytes; the network may drop it. This should never happen (the splitter keeps under it): report it.

CHAT_NOT_ARRIVING.title: messages sent by a subscriber are not arriving
CHAT_NOT_ARRIVING.explain: A subscriber sent messages over 30 s ago that the receiver has not rebuilt. Monitoring (its own route) still gets through and the receiver reports, so the room's chat route (its diode route, the chat port) is losing them. Shown on that route's wire, not on the receiver. After 15 min they are counted as lost.

checks.do: docker ps --filter name=<receiver> --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}} {{.Ports}}'   # running, and its published port (prod)
is that chat room's route up? (the monitoring route (CHAT|MONITOR) works)

CHAT_LOST.title: messages never reached the receiver
CHAT_LOST.explain: Messages a subscriber sent never arrived, even after 15 minutes. They are in that subscriber's sent log on the low-side host (low/logs/signal-udp-sent.jsonl).

RX_STALLED.title: the receiver's loop is stuck
RX_STALLED.explain: The receiver's main loop has not come round for 20 s. While it is stuck nothing is received and packets pile up, then get dropped. 'stuck in' says where (often my_forward).

FORWARD_FAILED.title: my_forward fails: records don't reach the destination
FORWARD_FAILED.explain: The receiver's latest hand-off to the destination (my_forward: in prod the Gotham feed) failed: it raised an error or returned False. Those records did not go out; the console still got the message. The link to the destination is red while the latest hand-off fails and green again at the next one that works.

FORWARD_SLOW.title: my_forward is slow
FORWARD_SLOW.explain: my_forward took over 2 s. It runs in the receiver's loop, so nothing else is received meanwhile; with many messages, packets get dropped.

DELIVER_FAILED.title: the receiver can't deliver messages to the console
DELIVER_FAILED.explain: Rebuilt messages could not be posted to the console (8091) and were dropped from the console (my_forward still got them).

MESSAGE_LOST.title: messages were lost on the way through the diode
MESSAGE_LOST.explain: Not all packets of some messages arrived within 30 s, so the receiver gave up on them. The console shows a 'lost' notice. A burst, a full buffer, or the diode dropping packets.

PACKETS_MISSING.title: packets went missing on the way through the diode
PACKETS_MISSING.explain: A gap in a room's packet numbers: some packets never reached its receiver. The receiver waits up to 30 s for them; if they don't come, the messages they belonged to are lost (a 'lost' notice). A burst, a full buffer, or the diode dropping packets.

MESSAGE_BROKEN.title: complete messages could not be rebuilt
MESSAGE_BROKEN.explain: All packets arrived but the message could not be decoded: corrupted on the way, or a sender with a different format.

checks.do: docker logs --since 1h <receiver> 2>&1 | grep -i 'could not be rebuilt'

RX_OVERFLOW.title: the receiver's buffer overflowed
RX_OVERFLOW.explain: The kernel dropped packets because the receiver's buffer was full: it was busy (slow my_forward or the console) during a burst.

BAD_PACKET.title: packets that are not relay packets arrive on the chat port
BAD_PACKET.explain: Something other than our subscribers sends to its room's route, or packets arrive damaged.

NOTICE_FAILED.title: lost-message notices could not reach the console
NOTICE_FAILED.explain: The receiver could not pass a 'message lost' notice to the console.

DB_ERROR.title: the console's database gives errors
DB_ERROR.explain: The console could not read or write relay.db (disk full, locked, or damaged). Chat, incidents or monitoring may not be saved.

CHECKS_FAILING.title: the console's monitoring checks are failing
CHECKS_FAILING.explain: Part of the Monitor tab's checks failed several times in a row (a bug or bad data). What the tab shows may be out of date.

checks.do: docker logs --since 15m signal-console 2>&1 | grep -A8 'check failed' | tail -40

LOOP_LAG.title: the console was blocked
LOOP_LAG.explain: The console's event loop was blocked for over 2 s (usually a slow disk). Pages and intake waited meanwhile.

INGEST_FAILED.title: the console failed to take in data
INGEST_FAILED.explain: The console failed (server error) on something the receiver or monitor-receiver sent.

checks.do: docker logs --since 1h signal-console 2>&1 | grep -A8 'Could not take in' | tail -40

AI_FAILED.title: the Analyst fails
AI_FAILED.explain: Asking the Analyst (relay-assist) failed (it is down, the model did not answer, or timed out). Monitoring itself is not affected.

DISK_LOW.title: a right-side disk is nearly full
DISK_LOW.explain: Under 10% free on the disk of relay.db or the records log. When it fills, writes fail.

OTHER.title: an app logged errors nobody foresaw
OTHER.explain: Every warning and error is counted by code; these have no specific code yet. The app's own log says what they were. If it repeats, give it a code and a rule.

CONTAINER_MEM_HIGH.title: a container is close to its memory limit
CONTAINER_MEM_HIGH.explain: Over 85% of its memory limit is in use. If it reaches it, Docker kills it (out of memory).

CONTAINER_CPU_HIGH.title: a container uses a lot of CPU
CONTAINER_CPU_HIGH.explain: Over 90% CPU for 5 minutes. It may be stuck in a loop or overloaded.

CONTAINER_PIDS_HIGH.title: a container is close to its process limit
CONTAINER_PIDS_HIGH.explain: Over 85% of its pids limit: it may soon fail to start threads.

FACTS_UNAVAILABLE.title: container facts can't be read
FACTS_UNAVAILABLE.explain: signal-monitor can't read container-facts (it is down, or can't read Docker). Exit codes, restarts and resource use are not known meanwhile.

checks.do: cd low && docker compose up -d container-facts

SIGNAL_UNKNOWN.title: signal-cli's link to Signal's servers can't be seen
SIGNAL_UNKNOWN.explain: signal-cli's health report (image r2 and later) has seen no connection event at all since it started, so whether it is connected is unknown. Messages may still flow; check signal-cli's log. If this follows an image update, the health watcher may not match the new version's log events (a launcher fix is needed).

ROOM_MISMATCH.title: a receiver gets packets for a room it doesn't serve
ROOM_MISMATCH.explain: Each chat room has its own route through the diode, to its receiver. This receiver got packets for a room it does not serve, so it dropped them: they never reach the wrong Gotham room, but that room's messages are not delivered by this receiver. Either the diode's route for that room points at the wrong receiver, or the room is new and its receiver isn't set up yet.

checks.do: check its routes file: the room's CHAT|<ROOM> rule must point at the receiver whose ROOMS lists it

ROOM_UNSERVED.title: a subscriber sends a room that no receiver serves
ROOM_UNSERVED.explain: The subscriber sends this room's messages (its groups in low/routes.conf), but no receiver on the high side serves the room, so those messages go nowhere. Either the room's receiver is not set up (or was removed), or its short name differs between routes.conf and the receiver's ROOMS (they must match exactly, in capitals). The diode also needs a route for the room.

checks.do: check its routes file has CHAT|<ROOM> pointing at that room's receiver

SUBSCRIBER_TWICE.title: the same routes run in two subscribers at once
SUBSCRIBER_TWICE.explain: Two subscribers that are both running use the same ROUTES_FOR name from routes.conf, so they send the same groups to the same rooms: every message arrives twice (and Gotham gets it twice). Usually a subscriber was started on a second host, or a copied compose block kept the same ROUTES_FOR. Stop one of them.

CONTAINER_PAUSED.title: a container is frozen (paused)
CONTAINER_PAUSED.explain: Docker has paused the container (docker pause): its program is stopped in place and answers nothing until it is unpaused. Paused signal-cli: new messages wait on Signal's servers; paused subscriber: they wait in signal-cli's memory.

MONITOR_CHECK_FAILED.title: signal-monitor's check of signal-cli doesn't get through (signal-cli itself works)
MONITOR_CHECK_FAILED.explain: signal-monitor's health check of signal-cli fails, but a subscriber still reads signal-cli's event stream, so signal-cli runs: the problem is the check's path (signal-monitor's certificate, its line in low/gateway/clients.conf (name, or rights without check), its network) or signal-monitor itself. Chat keeps flowing; only signal-cli's own figures and its link to Signal are unknown meanwhile.

checks.do: grep -v '^#' low/gateway/clients.conf   # its certificate's name must be a line here (signal-monitor: with check)

SUB_STATUS_LOST.title: a subscriber's status doesn't reach signal-monitor (it runs)
SUB_STATUS_LOST.explain: container-facts says the subscriber's container runs, but signal-monitor has had no status from it for 35 s: its status packets (UDP 6520, this host's network) don't arrive, or MONITOR_ADDR points elsewhere. Its own state is unknown meanwhile; chat may still flow (see its room's wires).

MONRX_WAITING.title: monitoring messages wait at monitor-receiver
MONRX_WAITING.explain: monitor-receiver can't pass the monitoring messages it gets on to the console (the console is restarting, stopped or unreachable), so it holds them, in order, up to 1000, and passes them on when the console is back. Nothing is lost while it holds them.

MONRX_REFUSED.title: the console refused monitoring messages
MONRX_REFUSED.explain: monitor-receiver passed monitoring messages on, but the console refused them (an HTTP 4xx answer): they are dropped. Usually a message the console doesn't understand (versions out of step).

CHECK_SLOW.title: signal-monitor's check of signal-cli is slow
CHECK_SLOW.explain: signal-cli answered signal-monitor's health check, but took over 2 s: it is busy or short of CPU or memory. It still works.

NAMES_SLOW.title: signal-cli is slow to answer name lookups
NAMES_SLOW.explain: The subscriber asks signal-cli for display names (for mentions and quotes) beside sending, and one of those requests took over 5 s. Messages are not held up, but a mention may show without a name. signal-cli being slow to answer often goes with slow or late messages: it is busy, short of CPU or memory, or its account data is slow to read.

checks.do: docker logs --since 1h signal-subscriber 2>&1 | grep 'Looking up names took'
